get.description:
One collection with its items in order.

404 -- never 403 -- when the caller's level is insufficient, so the response
does not disclose that a private collection exists.

Two upstream calls, in this order and not the other: the viewer level must be
resolved against *this collection's* creator, and the creator is not known
until we ask. Reading the collection first and retrying would never work --
a `connections` collection 404s on the first call, so the creator id we would
need to earn access to it is exactly what the failed response does not
contain. The same shape as the attachment serve path.

post.description:
A text written here (`origin: hosted`, a draft or published at once), or
a record of a work published elsewhere (`origin: external`). An external
record whose identifier works-service already holds claims that record
instead of minting a duplicate; provenance is decided downstream, never
by the client. With an `Idempotency-Key`, a repeat of the same create --
a second click, a retry after a timeout -- answers with the work the first
one made instead of minting another (#96).

Gradient values carry a hyphen (`green-blue`), which is not a Python

one; nothing needs attribute access, since values arrive off the wire.

BylineInvite.description:
One name to put on a byline, as a client asks for it.

account, or is a connection of the inviter, and so is credited without an
answer. A client must not be able to say either: that would be
attribution without consent. This tier decides both, off profile-service
and social-service, and stamps them on the forwarded body.

`CollectionDetail.items` carries only a first page since 2026-08-15; this is

ContentLanguage.description:
Relayed verbatim from the domain service.

The contract is `docs/architecture/content-language.md`. The BFF neither
computes nor reshapes any member of it: `served`, `available` and `primary`
are the domain service's answers, and the frontend reads its canonical, its
hreflang set and its redirect decision from them. Recomputing any of it here
would fork the resolver, and the two copies would disagree the first time a
field fell back.

LanguageProficiency.description:
A language the person says they speak, and how well.

**`code` is what makes this data rather than a string.** The field shipped
with `name` only -- free text, so the stored values are "English", "French",
"German", "Russian": no code, nothing to match a search filter against,
nothing to render in another interface language, and no way to tell
"Chinese" from "Mandarin" from a typo. `code` is the fix, and `name` stays
beside it so the rows written before it still render.

**Validated against the whole catalogue, not the authorable set.** This is a
claim about a *person*, not content they authored: a researcher who speaks
Hungarian should be able to say so on a site that does not offer Hungarian
as a writing language. `is_authorable_language` is for the languages someone
may write in; this is not one of those fields.

Optional because the rows already in the database have no code and must keep
loading. A write that omits it is accepted and simply carries less.
LanguageProficiency.title: LanguageProficiency

License.description:
A licence, as a slug -- the spelling every source uses and the one
works-service stores and returns (WORKS-SERVICE-PLAN step 6). Until
step 10 this enum carried publications-service's underscore spellings
(`cc_by`); works-service still accepts those on input, so an older file
that spells a licence that way still publishes.

`cc-by-nd`, `cc-by-nc-nd` and `public-domain` are read values: a harvested
record or a book's expression carries them. An author cannot put their own
text in the public domain by ticking a box in most jurisdictions.
License.title: License

Life.description:
A historical person's life dates, relayed from profile-service, which
sends them only once the person has died.
Life.title: Life

LifeDate.description:
A date as the record gives it: `1642`, `1642-12` or `1642-12-25`, a
leading `-` for BC, in its calendar (#1477). No source per date
(HISTORIC-PROFILES H4).
LifeDate.title: LifeDate

MarkdownViewState.description:
A file face's converted markdown: on the page, kept off it, or absent.
Mirrors works-service's `MarkdownViewState`.
MarkdownViewState.title: MarkdownViewState

MentionTarget.description:
One entry of the `mentions` map: the person or organization a `@handle`
in a body names (people and organizations share `@`, HANDLES-UNIFY-PLAN).

`username` is the **current** handle, which is not necessarily the one the
body was written with -- profile-service resolves old handles through
UsernameHistory, so a rename heals every mention of that profile rather than
stranding it. The renderer links and labels the chip from this field; for
an organization it is the orgname. `kind` picks the chip's badge.
MentionTarget.title: MentionTarget

OrganizationCard.description:
An organization a work names -- its venue (`affiliated_org_id`) or its
owner (`owner_org_id`) -- resolved by the BFF. The five fields a top bar
and a link need; deliberately not `OrganizationSummary`, whose member
counts and claim state are the org page's business.
OrganizationCard.title: OrganizationCard

PrimaryFormat.description:
Which view of a file face the work page leads with: the file (default),
or the markdown with the file as its PDF view. Mirrors works-service's
`PrimaryFormat`.
PrimaryFormat.title: PrimaryFormat

ProfileImageCredit.description:
Who made the profile's photo and under which licence, as that licence
asks to be credited (HISTORIC-PROFILES H5). The photo is
`profile_image_url`, in our storage; there is never a source link.
ProfileImageCredit.title: ProfileImageCredit

ProfileMe.description: Owner view — every field, every visibility flag.
ProfileMe.title: ProfileMe

ProfilePublic.description: Public view — gated by is_public and per-field toggles.
ProfilePublic.title: ProfilePublic

ProfileStats.description:
Counts and tab-presence for the profile header (#1077).

Aggregated at the BFF per request from four services, never stored. Each
field is None when its leg failed, and the frontend treats None as
"unknown" -- it keeps the tab and drops the number -- never as zero or
empty. `followers_count` and `works_count` are the same for every viewer;
`has_cv` and `has_timetable` are resolved at the caller's real access
level, so they say whether *this* viewer would find anything on the tab.
ProfileStats.title: ProfileStats

Reference.description:
A bibliographic reference in a hosted text: a CSL-aligned snapshot that
may link to a known work or a library citation.
Reference.title: Reference

ReorderRequest.description: The full ordered list of entity ids. `position` becomes the index here.
ReorderRequest.title: ReorderRequest

ResolveResult.description: A DOI, arXiv id, ISBN or title, resolved index-first.
ResolveResult.title: ResolveResult

StatusNotice.description:
A notice in force: what was said, by whom (author, moderator, source),
and where. Who performed a moderator action is not exposed.
StatusNotice.title: StatusNotice

contents and its metadata are served with no body, and the reader is told
why -- with the other editions that do read here.

TikzRender.description: One materialised `:::tikz` diagram: its SVG, its dark-ink variant, its size.

WorkCard.description: What a list, a card or a search hit needs: the head row, no text.

WorkKind.description:
What kind of text we host -- a work's `kind` (WORKS-SERVICE-PLAN
decision 1). Named `PublicationType` until step 10; null on an external
record, which has only the world's `type`. Every kind libretimes.io may
create -- living content and, since 2026-09-14, the five citable record
types.

The record types are creatable here with the semantics works-service
enforces by type alone: frozen on
publish, numbered, retracted not deleted, corrected by a new version
(WORKS-UNIFICATION decision 15). The chooser says so before Publish.

See docs/architecture/content-types.md.
WorkKind.title: WorkKind

WorkOut.description: One work, read: the head row, the served text, the byline, the status.

WorkReferenceIn.description:
One author-added reference on an external record: a pick from the
index (`cited_work_id`) or a custom entry. A custom entry links itself if
the cited work is harvested later, but only by identifier -- never by
title -- which is why the composer asks for a DOI.

WorkType.description:
The world's vocabulary (ORCID/CSL/Crossref): what an export reads.
Every work has one; a hosted text's is mapped from its `kind` on write.
WorkType.title: WorkType

WorkUpdate.description:
PATCH a work. Lifecycle is never a PATCH field -- publishing,
unpublishing and withdrawing are verbs. Which fields a caller may send,
and which apply to which origin, is works-service's.
WorkUpdate.title: WorkUpdate
